claim: For any codespace (or other ephemeral-compute) PoC, the FIRST success criterion is an evidence-branch push to the canonical repo from inside the ephemeral environment — before any deeper exec work. Cost note: stop the codespace FIRST at any stall — hourly compute bleeds during debugging; storage continues after stop at lower rate.

claim: A pre-registration seal pushed before the run makes the RUN's meaning survive the runner's death. Three wave-69 deaths, three recoveries of increasing elegance: (1) 69-a committed its battery+promotion-law pre-run (21b4859) — the keeper ran the dead lane's own scripts verbatim; (2) 69-b finished the engineering in three repos but died pre-commit — the finisher audited-then-pushed with zero fixes needed (broken inventory EMPTY); (3) 69-d sealed AND ran R1 (12 calls) then died — the finisher spent 0 new calls, instead re-derived every recorded metric offline through the unchanged instrument (verify-then-adopt, 18/18) and ran only the missing R3. Pattern: when a lane dies, its sealed artifacts are EVIDENCE, not suggestions — re-executing what the seal already covers is double-spend; the finisher's real work is epistemics (prove the recorded numbers re-derive) plus completing only what the seal does not cover.
